findings.category: 未宣言の前提への依存
findings.message: `serve` hard-codes the OS bind endpoint to `127.0.0.1:3000`, but neither the spec nor the project environment declaration records the required loopback/port assumption or its configuration policy. This makes deployment depend on an undeclared address and port-availability contract; declare the endpoint or inject/configure it before binding.

`AuthHttpApi::serve` is the public driver entrypoint but returns `HttpServerOutcome`, directly violating the cli_driver rule that public `handle` or equivalent operations render to `CommandOutcome`. This leaves lifecycle errors outside the primary-adapter rendering boundary; return a `CommandOutcome` with failure/exit semantics or move server lifecycle ownership to the appropriate composition boundary.

The real server cannot produce the lifecycle outcomes this code claims to map. Axum 0.8.9 documents that `axum::serve` without graceful shutdown never completes or returns an error, so `map_server_result` is only exercised by the synthetic ready-future test; after a successful bind, `serve` can return neither `Stopped` nor `Failed`. Add an actual shutdown future/configurable runner and test the integrated path. See the [axum 0.8.9 serve contract](https://docs.rs/axum/0.8.9/axum/fn.serve.html).

findings.category: 未宣言の前提への依存
findings.message: The test treats any 100 ms timeout as proof that binding succeeded and the Axum serve loop began. It also passes when the future was not polled far enough or bind/setup has not completed, so its conclusion depends on an undeclared scheduler and loopback-bind timing assumption. Signal readiness after a successful bind, or inject a pre-bound listener, before applying the timeout to the serve loop.

findings.category: 未宣言の前提への依存
findings.message: The shutdown future discards `tokio::signal::ctrl_c()`'s `Result`. If signal-listener registration fails, the future completes immediately, Axum interprets that as a graceful-shutdown request, and `serve` returns a successful `CommandOutcome` instead of reporting the infrastructure failure. This depends on the undeclared assumption that signal registration is infallible; preserve the error and map it to `HttpServerOutcome::Failed`. The [Tokio API](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.52.3/tokio/signal/fn.ctrl_c.html) explicitly returns `io::Result<()>`.

A successful `TcpStream::connect` does not prove that Axum accepted the connection: the listener is already bound before the server task starts, so the kernel can complete and queue the connection while the task has not reached `accept`. The test then drops the stream and requests shutdown, allowing it to pass without exercising Axum's accept/request path. Send a request and await its response, or instrument server-side acceptance, before signaling shutdown. Tokio's listener documentation notes that connections can wait in the [accept queue](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.52.3/tokio/net/struct.TcpListener.html).

`HttpServerOutcome` is described by the briefing as an internal lifecycle DTO and is no longer returned by any public operation, but it remains publicly exported as `cli_driver::auth::HttpServerOutcome`. This exposes an adapter-internal transport lifecycle type and permits consumers to couple to or construct it despite the public `CommandOutcome` boundary. Make it private or `pub(crate)`.

findings.category: 未宣言の前提への依存
findings.message: The readiness test assumes one TCP `read` returns the complete `HTTP/1.1` prefix. `AsyncReadExt::read` only promises to pull some available bytes, so a valid response fragmented before the eighth byte makes this test fail nondeterministically. This transport-boundary assumption is undeclared; use `read_exact` for the fixed prefix or accumulate through the header terminator. See Tokio’s [`AsyncReadExt`](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.52.3/tokio/io/trait.AsyncReadExt.html).

`cargo fmt --check -p cli_driver` exits 1 and reports multiple formatting differences in this file, so the repository's `fmt-check` dependency causes `cargo make ci-rust` to fail. Run rustfmt on the scoped source before approval.

`PasswordHash::new` validates only the `$argon2id$` prefix, so values such as `$argon2id$` or `$argon2id$garbage` become a `PasswordHash` even though the declared stored format is a complete PHC argon2id encoding with valid version/parameters/salt/digest. This breaks the newtype's documented validated-encoding invariant and lets malformed persisted hashes cross the domain boundary; validate the full PHC representation or reject malformed encodings.

`is_complete_argon2id_phc` checks only that salt and digest are non-empty; it accepts malformed PHC payloads such as `$argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$%%%$%%%`. The project’s declared encoding policy requires salt and digest to be unpadded Base64, so `PasswordHash::new` still admits an invalid stored hash. Validate the salt and digest encoding before constructing the value.

This template distribution file now ships consumer-specific platform, protocol, Argon2, repository, and concurrency defaults, contradicting its own consumer-ownership rules at lines 20, 75, and 117. Keep these values in the consumer-owned declaration instance, or separately record and implement an explicit decision to promote them to shared template defaults.

The declared lifecycle does not match the current `AuthHttpApi::serve` path. It awaits bare axum 0.8 `serve`, whose future never completes or returns an error after a successful bind; accept errors are retried internally. Consequently this path cannot produce `Stopped` or a serve-time `Failed`, and cancellation/process termination drops the future without returning either outcome. Describe the actual lifecycle (with only bind failure returned), or wire an explicit graceful-shutdown/fallible serving mechanism before declaring these outcomes.

The declared Ctrl-C lifecycle still does not match `AuthHttpApi::serve`: the shutdown future discards the `io::Result` from `tokio::signal::ctrl_c()`, so signal-listener setup failure completes the shutdown future immediately and is rendered as `Stopped` / `CommandOutcome { success: true }` without any Ctrl-C. Conversely, axum 0.8's `with_graceful_shutdown` future does not return a serve error, so the documented serve-error-to-`Failed` path is not real. Handle signal setup failure as `Failed` and describe the reachable failure sources accurately, or revise the declaration to state the actual behavior.

T003 and T004 are both ready at the T002 dependency frontier, have distinct usecase ownership, and their combined estimate is 400 lines (180 + 220), within the 500-line ceiling. Splitting them across B001 and B002 is avoidable: T004 can replace T003 in B001 and T003 can run before T006 in B002, preserving dependencies and leaving each batch within scope ceilings.

The `plan` object has no `summary`, leaving GO-001 without the required plan-owned goal-to-task traceability. Add a target + operation + GO-001 summary linking the contributing tasks, including `composition`/T007, without restating upstream behavior.

T001's attribution list omits the reference catalogue entries `domain::Username` and `domain::UsernameError`; both remain orphaned even though reference entries require an owner. Attribute them to an appropriate convergence task such as T001 without implying that the task modifies them.

T006 bundles two independently verifiable behavior units while still `todo`: the registration HTTP slice (`RegisterRequest`, IN-001/AC-001) and the login/token HTTP slice (`LoginRequest`, `AccessTokenResponse`, IN-002/AC-002). Split these into dependent executable tasks, assigning the shared `AuthHttpApi`/`HttpServerOutcome` foundation once and retaining the applicable CN-003/CN-004/CN-005 anchors.

T006 is ordered in B001 before T003, but T006 implements `AuthHttpApi`, whose catalogued constructor requires `RegisterUserService`; that service is created by T003 in later B002. The batch order therefore requires T006 to refer to an artifact not yet created. Move T006 after T003 (while preserving the ceiling split).

`verify` accepts attacker-/storage-controlled Argon2 parameters and allocates `params.block_count()` blocks without an application-level bound. A hash containing an extreme `m` value can trigger multi-terabyte allocation/OOM during login. Enforce a bounded parameter policy before allocation and reject hashes outside it.

This adapter newly depends on undeclared external assumptions: OS CSPRNG availability, PHC/base64 encoding details, Argon2 memory/time limits, and the `RwLock` concurrency model. `knowledge/conventions/environment-assumptions.md` still contains TODO declarations, while neither the spec nor an environment declaration records these assumptions. Declare the applicable platform, encoding, resource, and concurrency constraints.

The Argon2 parameter cap does not bound the PHC digest length. `decode_vec` and the subsequent `vec![0; parsed.digest.len()]` accept an arbitrarily large stored hash payload, allowing memory exhaustion before Argon2 runs. Enforce the declared 32-byte digest (and 16-byte salt) limits before decoding/allocation.

The pre-decode limits use padded-Base64 lengths, but the fields are decoded as unpadded Base64. A 23-character salt decodes to 17 bytes yet passes the 24-character guard, and a 44-character digest decodes to 33 bytes yet passes the 44-character guard. `decode_vec` therefore allocates oversized fields before the later byte-length check rejects them, contrary to the briefing and environment declaration. Use the exact unpadded maxima (22 and 43 characters) and test these boundary cases.

findings.category: 未宣言の前提への依存 / unbounded encoding parse
findings.message: `parse_encoded_hash` has no total PHC or parameter-field length guard before splitting and parsing the stored encoding. For example, an otherwise valid `m` value can contain arbitrarily many leading zeroes, forcing unbounded scans on every verification while still parsing below the numeric cap. The environment declaration bounds numeric parameters and salt/digest sizes but does not declare a bound for their textual PHC representation. Add a fail-closed encoded-length bound before parsing, or declare and enforce an equivalent input boundary.
The voluntary binding for `LoginError` points to a test that only covers the successful `Ok` path and never produces or checks a `LoginError`. Bind it to an error-path test or add suitable coverage.

The `CredentialParseError`→IN-001 edge is still a `voluntary_binding`, but its cited test only verifies empty-password parse rejection and cannot prove IN-001's success promise (“Register a user through the API”). Convert this error-type edge to a waiver with a non-empty ownership reason; CN-005 remains directly covered by the `PasswordInputError` binding.

`PasswordHashError` is recorded as a voluntary binding for CN-001, but it only represents invalid password-hash construction. CN-001's success promise is Argon2id password-hash storage, which is covered by `PasswordHash`, `PasswordHasher`, and `Argon2PasswordAdapter`; this error edge should be a waiver with a non-empty reason.

The new `CredentialParseError`→IN-001 waiver is rejected by the current obligation evaluator, and `bin/sotp test-obligation check` exits 1 for this edge. The declared error specifically covers registration credential parsing, so this reason does not establish that the edge has no verifiable IN-001 behavior. Bind the relevant behavior or correct the upstream edge; the current record leaves the track gate failing.

`PasswordHashError`→CN-001 is recorded as a waiver even though `InvalidEncoding` has directly verifiable behavior against CN-001's argon2id requirement. The obligation evaluator rejects this waiver and the required check fails. Restore a voluntary binding to the existing non-argon2id rejection test or correct the upstream edge.

The `CredentialParseError`→IN-001 voluntary binding cites only a command-parsing test and never exercises registration through the API, so it does not verify IN-001's central behavior. The evaluator reports `CentralUnverified`, leaving the DonePending obligation gate failing. Add API-level evidence or correct/refine the upstream edge instead of treating this parsing test as fulfillment.

The AuthHttpApi→CN-003 binding has a stale fulfillment verdict after its bound test bodies changed. `bin/sotp test-obligation check` now exits 1 with `TestChanged` drift (and results reports one stale Done obligation), so the required obligation gate is no longer green. Re-run the canonical obligation evaluation for the changed tests and ensure `check` passes, repairing the binding if the verifier rejects it.

findings.category: goal not anchored to a decision
findings.message: GO-001 combines registration, credential authentication, and token issuance, but its sole cited decision only selects opaque tokens after authentication. The separate registration ADR is not cited here, and no cited decision establishes login-attempt authentication as a capability, so the goal exceeds its decision anchors.

findings.category: missing AC coverage for a stated goal
findings.message: GO-001 requires authenticating login attempts, but AC-002 only checks token issuance once a login is already described as successful. No acceptance criterion deterministically proves that supplied credentials are verified or that invalid credentials are rejected, leaving the authentication part of the goal uncovered.

findings.category: 未宣言の前提への依存
findings.message: CN-003 introduces an external HTTP boundary for registration and login, while the project-owned environment declaration still contains TODOs for accepted input encoding, resource limits, and concurrency behavior, and the spec records none of those assumptions. Downstream design would have to invent boundary behavior for malformed/oversized inputs and concurrent access.

findings.category: 未宣言の前提への依存
findings.message: CN-002 keeps every user and token in process memory, but CN-005 and CN-006 limit only individual request bodies and concurrent requests. Sequential registrations and token issuances can therefore grow retained state without any declared capacity/retention boundary or defined failure behavior when memory is exhausted; the project environment declaration still leaves resource limits as TODO.

CN-007 contradicts IN-002 and AC-002: those elements require token issuance after successful authentication/login, while CN-007 says a successful login is rejected at token capacity and no token is written. The contract therefore gives mutually exclusive outcomes for the same successful-authentication case.

findings.category: 未宣言の前提への依存
findings.message: CN-004 defines UTF-8 decoding and malformed-input handling but leaves Unicode normalization unspecified while the project environment declaration’s normalization field remains TODO. Registration and authentication can therefore disagree across downstream implementations about whether canonically equivalent credential strings are identical, so the external input contract still depends on an undeclared normalization policy.

`usecase::IssuedAccessToken` is declared as a `ValueObject`, but its contract only describes an application-boundary serialization proof and declares no invariant, ubiquitous-language meaning, or invariant ownership. This supports a DTO/boundary-carrier role, not a usecase value-object role.

`domain::AccessTokenRepository` (`save`, `find`) and `domain::UserRepository` (`find_by_username`, `save`) declare every persistence operation as synchronous. Because CN-002 explicitly makes these ports replaceable, a future database-backed adapter would have to block or change the port and propagate that change through the usecase layer; neither entry documents or justifies this synchronous contract.

`domain::UserRepository::find_by_username` returns the shared `UserRepositoryError`, including `DuplicateUser`, even though that write-conflict variant cannot arise from a lookup. The entry does not document a producible subset, so every lookup caller must handle a write-only error variant.

`usecase::PasswordHasher` cites only IN-002, but its `hash` method creates a stored password hash and correctly cites CN-001; registration is the consuming operation, while login uses `PasswordVerifier`. The entry-level IN-002 reference is therefore off-topic and should be replaced with the registration/hashing anchors.

`usecase::LoginCommandError` and `usecase::RegisterUserCommandError` independently declare the identical `InvalidUsername(domain::UsernameError)` and `InvalidPassword(PasswordInputError)` shape. Neither is shared or references a common declaration, so the same credential-parsing error contract must be maintained twice.

The docs for `domain::AccessTokenRepository` and `domain::UserRepository` paraphrase CN-002's in-memory-behind-a-replaceable-port decision (`the in-memory implementation is replaceable`) instead of limiting themselves to the type purpose and an anchor citation. This violates `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`usecase::LoginService` and `usecase::RegisterUserService` declare async `execute` methods but `cli_driver::AuthHttpApi::new` requires them as `Arc<dyn …>`; likewise `domain::UserRepository` and `domain::AccessTokenRepository` declare async methods while both interactors require `Arc<dyn …>`. An async trait method has an opaque future return and is not dyn-compatible, so these declared object types cannot be constructed. An `async_trait`-style transformation would instead expose a boxed-future signature not represented by this catalogue. Use static dispatch or declare an object-safe future-returning contract. See the [Rust Reference](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

`usecase::PlaintextPassword` repeats CN-005's behavior as prose—“empty input is rejected”—even though its invariant and methods already carry the CN-005 references. `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md` requires an anchor citation or short identifying noun phrase instead of restating the behavioral contract.

`usecase::PasswordInputError` docs restate the upstream password-length behavior in prose (`empty or exceeds the declared UTF-8 byte limit`) instead of using an anchor cite, violating the no-upstream-restatement policy. Keep the docs as an anchor-based type-purpose reference.

`cli_driver::AuthHttpApi::new` still declares `login: Arc<dyn usecase::auth::LoginService>`, but its sole method-level reference is IN-001, which concerns registration. Removing IN-002 from this method leaves the login dependency without a relevant spec trace; the briefing only justifies removing the deferred reference at entry level. Restore IN-002 on `new` (or remove the login dependency from the declared foundation shape until T009).

findings.category: 未宣言の前提への依存
findings.message: `PlaintextPassword::parse` copies the entire caller-provided password into a `String` without any size bound or defined excess behavior. Both registration and login therefore depend on an undeclared input/resource limit; `knowledge/conventions/environment-assumptions.md` still leaves resource limits as TODO, so oversized requests can cause unbounded allocation before hashing or verification.
